question: A shared services group wants to take a Claude-assisted purchase-request triage from an idea to everyday use across eight teams. Which sequence of steps is correct?
options: A) Extend to the other teams with the checks that proved necessary; pick one team and a bounded slice of requests; run it alongside the existing process for a month; compare the two sets of results and fix what failed.

B) Run it alongside the existing process for a month; compare the two sets of results and fix what failed; pick one team and a bounded slice of requests; extend to the other teams with the checks that proved necessary.

C) Pick one team and a bounded slice of requests; run it alongside the existing process for a month; compare the two sets of results and fix what failed; extend to the other teams with the checks that proved necessary.

D) Compare the two sets of results and fix what failed; pick one team and a bounded slice of requests; extend to the other teams with the checks that proved necessary; run it alongside the existing process for a month.
correct_answers: C) Pick one team and a bounded slice of requests; run it alongside the existing process for a month; compare the two sets of results and fix what failed; extend to the other teams with the checks that proved necessary.
explanations: Extending to every team first is a full rollout before any evidence exists, which makes the later pilot and comparison pointless because the risk has already been taken.
Running alongside the existing process before choosing a team and a slice means the trial has no defined scope, and the scoping decision arrives after the comparison it was supposed to make possible.

Correct. A bounded slice on one team keeps early mistakes cheap, running alongside the existing process gives a fair comparison rather than an impression, fixing what failed happens while the scope is still small, and the wider rollout then carries the human checks the comparison showed were needed.
There are no results to compare at the start, and the parallel run that would have produced them is left until after the arrangement has already been extended to all eight teams.
